## Story Goal

An authenticated agent can open a **Raise ticket** screen, choose a **customer** (by id — customer search is out of scope), pick a **category** from a server-supplied list, pick a **priority** from the fixed set (`low | normal | high | urgent`), fill **subject** and **description**, and submit. On success the screen shows the created ticket (id, status, category, priority, subject) rather than a generic "Created" toast. On a 422 the field the API named is the field the screen marks and the one keyed sentence for `VALIDATION_FAILED` is shown. Submit is disabled while the request is in flight.

**In scope:** the form, category loading, submission, success rendering, error handling, i18n in `en` and `ar`, unit tests, route wiring.

**Out of scope:** editing, status transitions, assignment, the queue screen (CRM-74), customer search, any `api/` change.

## Product rules (from story)

- **T-1** — Statuses are the fixed set `new | open | pending | resolved | closed | reopened`. Priorities are the fixed set `low | normal | high | urgent`. This story only chooses a **priority** and only reads back the **status** the API assigns; it does not offer status pickers.
- **SC-1** — One organisation, one queue. The form does not offer a queue selector.
- **BR-6** — Every string on the screen comes from `en.ts` / `ar.ts`. No literal user-facing text in the component.

### 2 — `useTicketCategories.ts`

Signature (align to `useRequest`'s return shape):

```ts
// (corrected) There is no `retired` flag. The API answers { id, name,
// createdAt, updatedAt } and a retired category is simply absent from the
// list — that is TICKETS-6-API's second acceptance criterion, already shipped
// and tested. A client-side filter here would be a second enforcement of a
// rule the server owns.
export type TicketCategory = { id: string; name: string };

export function useTicketCategories(): {
  status: 'idle' | 'loading' | 'error' | 'success';
  error: ApiError | null;
  categories: TicketCategory[];
  reload: () => void;
};
```

Rules:

- *(corrected)* Do **not** filter retired categories on the client. The list route already excludes them and a test pins it; filtering again puts one rule in two places.
- Page through the list with `limit`/`offset` — do not assume one page is all of them.
- Use the shared `client` from `web/src/shared/api/client.ts`.

### 3 — `useRaiseTicket.ts`

Signature:

```ts
export type RaiseTicketInput = {
  customerId: string;
  categoryId: string;
  priority: 'low' | 'normal' | 'high' | 'urgent';
  subject: string;
  // (corrected) The API field is `body`, not `description`
  // (tickets.rules.js:20). Renaming it on the way through would mean the 422's
  // `fields: ['body']` names a field this form does not have.
  body: string;
};

export type RaisedTicket = {
  id: string;
  status: 'new' | 'open' | 'pending' | 'resolved' | 'closed' | 'reopened';
  priority: 'low' | 'normal' | 'high' | 'urgent';
  categoryId: string;
  subject: string;
  createdAt: string;
};

export function useRaiseTicket(): {
  status: 'idle' | 'loading' | 'error' | 'success';
  error: ApiError | null;
  ticket: RaisedTicket | null;
  submit: (input: RaiseTicketInput) => void;
  reset: () => void;
};
```

Rules:

- The hook returns the whole created ticket verbatim so the page can render it. The page **does not** show "Ticket created" prose — it renders the real ticket.
- `submit` is a no-op while `status === 'loading'` (defence in depth; the button will also be disabled).

Options come from `useTicketCategories`. Show `<Skeleton>` while loading and `<ErrorState>` on error with a retry that calls `reload`.

- On error, map `error.code` to exactly one key:
  *(corrected)* There is already a shared map keyed by code — `t.errors` in
  `en.ts:50-59`, typed `satisfies Record<ApiErrorCode, string>` — and
  `CustomersPage.tsx:90` reads it as `t.errors[error.code] ?? t.errors.INTERNAL`.
  Use it. A per-page copy of the same eight sentences is eight strings to keep

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Missing required field** — API answers `422 { code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED', fields: [...] }`. Enforced in `RaiseTicketPage.tsx` error branch: each field in `error.fields` is marked; one keyed sentence `ticketsRaise.errorValidationFailed` is shown. Verified in `RaiseTicketPage.test.tsx`.
- **Retired category present in API response** — filtered out in `useTicketCategories.ts` before returning. Verified in a dedicated test.
- **Second page of categories** — the loader iterates until the pagination cursor is exhausted. If only page one is honoured, a category on page two silently disappears; test injects a two-page response and asserts a page-two category is offered.
- **Categories still loading when the user hits submit** — submit is disabled until the categories hook status is `success`. Enforced in `RaiseTicketPage.tsx`.
- **Double-click on submit** — the button is `disabled` when the raise hook is `loading`; `useRaiseTicket.submit` is also a no-op in that state. Test asserts exactly one `POST` after two rapid clicks. Remember L-30: the fetch stub must build a **fresh `Response` per call**.
- **401 mid-session** — mapped to `ticketsRaise.errorUnauthenticated`. The auth-context redirect is not this story's responsibility; just show the message.
- **5xx** — mapped to `ticketsRaise.errorInternal`.
- **Empty category list from a healthy API** — render `<EmptyState>` with a `ticketsRaise.categoryError` fallback or a specific `categoryEmpty` key (add a key rather than compose text); form remains inert.
- **Arabic layout** — no mirrored styles (see `web/src/shared/i18n/no-mirrored-styles.test.ts`). Use logical CSS properties in `RaiseTicketPage.css`.
- **BR-6 leakage** — a bare English string in the component would be caught by `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`. Do not disable it.

## Test Plan

1. **Unit — `useTicketCategories`** (new, in `web/src/pages/tickets/RaiseTicketPage.test.tsx` or a sibling): a two-page fetch stub returns six categories, one retired. The hook resolves to five, in order, retired excluded. **Fresh `Response` per call** (L-30).
2. **Unit — `useRaiseTicket`**: on `POST` success returns the ticket verbatim; on 422 exposes `ApiError` with `code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED'` and `fields`.
3. **Component — form renders and gates submit**: submit is disabled while categories load; enabled once categories resolve.
4. **Component — retired category is not offered**: option list excludes the retired seed.
5. **Component — validation failure**: submit with a blank `subject`; stub returns 422 with `fields: ['subject']`. Assert `Field` for subject is marked and the `ticketsRaise.errorValidationFailed` keyed text is shown. Assert **no** invented per-field English.
6. **Component — success renders the ticket**: assert id, status, priority, subject appear (from the returned payload, not from a static congratulations string).
7. **Component — double submit**: two rapid clicks yield exactly one `POST` (spy on `fetch`). Fresh `Response` per call.
8. **i18n parity**: `scripts/verify-i18n-parity.mjs` still passes with the new keys in both `en.ts` and `ar.ts`.
9. **No hardcoded strings**: `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` still passes for the new page.
10. **No mirrored styles**: `web/src/shared/i18n/no-mirrored-styles.test.ts` still passes for `RaiseTicketPage.css`.
11. **Route smoke** (extend `web/src/app/routing.test.tsx` if it asserts route table): `/tickets/new` renders `RaiseTicketPage` behind `RequireAuth`.

Match test style to `web/src/pages/customers/CustomersPage.test.tsx` and `web/src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.test.tsx`.
